newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian prison officers strike over staffing.
newsitem.headline: Belgian prison officers strike over staffing.

text.p: Belgium's prison officers began a 24-hour strike on Tuesday in protest at low staffing levels, a problem they said had been exacerbated by the country's child abduction, sexual abuse and murder scandal, Belgian radio said.

It said that since mid-August when two girls were rescued and the bodies of four others discovered on properties belonging to convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux, the number of arrests had risen and the number of conditional releases declined.
So far 13 people have been arrested in connection with the affair, although most have been questioned and released as the main enquiries progress.
Dutroux was arrested in August with four others -- including his second wife -- in connection with the discovery of the bodies of the dead girls.

Seven other people, including a former federal government minister, have also been arrested in connection with the 1991 murder of francophone Socialist Party patriarch Andre Cools. They too are still in jail.
There are just over 4,000 prison officers in Belgium guarding roughly double the number of prisoners.
The officers are demanding that more prisons be built, that existing ones be refurbished and that more people who are not a danger to the public be conditionally released.
Early on Tuesday the strike was going ahead peacefully, with gendarmes guarding the prisons in place of warders.
